answer: Persistent Operator Ledger. Each new identity must post a small refundable deposit, but refunds clear only after a 90-day delay recorded in a shared ledger keyed to the operator's payout address. Duplicate clusters draining deposits trigger a withdrawal spiral: payouts freeze and prior deposits forfeit. An attacker running N identities locks N deposits and loses all on detection. A jetty rule caps same-operator outflow per epoch, and a cedar flag marks repeat offenders.
